derivations.claim: Lift $X$ to the cut manifold $N$. The interior lifts without identification because it misses $F_E$. Along $\beta$, the disk selects a continuous side of $F_E$, giving one lift of this arc to $P$. The other boundary arc lifts into a single annulus $A_i$, since the interior of $\alpha$ misses the boundary curves of $F_E$. Thus the lifted disk is properly embedded, with one boundary arc in $P$ and the other a proper embedded arc of $A_i$.

A proper embedded arc in an annulus either has both endpoints on the same boundary circle and cuts off a disk, or joins the two boundary circles. To see this directly, cut the annulus along an arc joining its boundary circles and unwrap its translates to a strip. A lift of the given embedded arc has disjoint integer translates. If both ends lie on the same edge of the strip, the interval between them on that edge and the lifted arc bound a disk on the strip side; the interior of this disk cannot meet a translate of the arc, since an innermost such translate would have interlaced endpoints, forcing an intersection. This disk therefore projects injectively to a disk in the annulus. If the endpoints lie on different edges, the arc is a spanning arc. Cutting along a spanning arc gives a disk, so its position is a product arc in some product parametrization of the annulus.

The same-boundary case is impossible here. Its annular disk descends to a disk $Q$ in the boundary torus, with boundary $\alpha\cup\eta$, where $\eta$ is an arc of $\partial F_E$; its interior misses $\partial F_E$. Join $X$ and $Q$ along $\alpha$ and push the interior slightly off the torus. The result has boundary $\beta\cup\eta$ and interior disjoint from $F_E$. Both endpoints of the lifted $\alpha$ lie on the same boundary circle of $A_i$, so the selected side of $F_E$ at the two ends agrees along $\eta$. In a thin boundary collar of $F_E$, move the portion $\eta$ slightly into $F_E$, simultaneously adjusting the disk near that portion; this gives a disk whose simple closed boundary $\gamma$ lies in the interior of $F_E$. By [F1], $\gamma$ bounds a disk in $F_E$. The collar between $\eta$ and its displaced copy adjoins to that disk, yielding a disk in $F_E$ bounded by $\beta$ and a boundary arc. Thus $\beta$ is boundary-parallel by [F2], a contradiction.

Therefore the annular arc joins the two boundary circles. By the product parametrization in step 2.1, a core of $A_i$ can be chosen to meet this arc transversely once. Any two cores of an annulus are isotopic: cut along a spanning arc and straighten a core in the resulting disk, then reglue. Apply the inverse of such a core isotopy to the annular arc, and extend this boundary isotopy to a collar in $N$, moving the lifted disk with it. The resulting disk meets the prescribed $s_i$ once along its boundary. Its remaining boundary arc lies in $P$, so it misses every other $s_j$. This gives the required $\widetilde X$.

If there are no one-suture disks in $N$, step 4.1 rules out every exterior boundary-compressing disk. Combined with the assumed geometric incompressibility, this is the stated essentiality conclusion. The argument never restricts the longitudinal winding of $\alpha$; a spanning arc may wind before it meets the core once. It therefore does not identify arbitrary exterior boundary compression with meridional boundary compression of a spanning surface.
